doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Quebec and the move to New York
title: Touring with Carmen McRae and arriving in New York, 1958
summary: He went on the road with Carmen, stayed in New York in February 1958, and was blocked by the union transfer rule. The union controlled where members lived and worked.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well you certainly could get that here.

Oh, can you ever get it here. I found out, that’s for sure. But anyhow I went on the road with Carmen. I left Ottawa and went with Carmen. I went to Chicago and a few other places with her and it was nice. I ended up in New York. So she decided to stay in New York for a little while. And I made some things with her around the New York area. And then I left. I was supposed to be going back to California but I decided not to. I had to start somewhere.

This is ’58. The winter, like February of ’58. And the union wouldn’t allow me to work because I came in on a transfer, in those days you had to transfer. You had to resign from your original local and join outright. I didn’t want to do that, so I had to wait three to six months before I could work anywhere. They could let me work a few places, in Harlem or Brooklyn or something.
I mean they were very powerful at the time, weren’t they?

Very powerful. They would call to make sure that you were still living at whatever address you gave them, make sure you didn’t go out on the road with a band or whatever. You had to stay in the city. Those were more dues.
